title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 218 (Protection of employees during investigation)

content.overview: Section 218 provides that notwithstanding anything contained in any other law, during the course of any investigation under Chapter XIV, if any employee of a company provides information during such investigation, the company shall not, without the prior approval of the Tribunal, discharge, remove, suspend, demote or otherwise reduce in rank or status, or punish by any other means, such employee, or change the terms of employment to his disadvantage. The protection is for the period the section states and is aimed at preventing victimisation of employees who cooperate with the investigation. It is not a general bar on ordinary discipline wholly unrelated to the investigation.
content.glance: During investigation: company needs Tribunal prior approval to discharge, suspend, demote, punish or disadvantage an employee who has provided information; anti-victimisation rule, not a blanket ban on all discipline.
content.study: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, if any employee of a company provides information during investigation under this Chapter, the company shall not discharge, remove, dismiss, suspend, demote or otherwise reduce in rank or status, or punish by any other means, such employee, or change the terms of employment of such employee to his disadvantage, except with the previous approval of the Tribunal. Current-law framing: confirm an ongoing investigation under the Chapter; identify an employee who provided information; require prior Tribunal approval before adverse employment action; distinguish ordinary discipline unconnected with the investigation cooperation.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: Employee has provided information during an investigation under Chapter XIV.

sections.heading: Protected Actions
sections.body: Company shall not, without prior Tribunal approval, discharge, remove, dismiss, suspend, demote, reduce in rank/status, punish, or change terms to the employee’s disadvantage.

sections.heading: Approval
sections.body: Prior approval of the Tribunal is required for any such adverse action.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.body: Aimed at preventing victimisation for cooperation; not a general freeze on all ordinary discipline unrelated to the investigation.

examples.title: Dismissal after cooperation
examples.body: An accounts manager gives documents to an inspector under s. 217. The company then dismisses him without Tribunal approval. Section 218 is breached if the dismissal is of an employee who provided information during the investigation.

examples.title: Tribunal approval obtained
examples.body: The company seeks and obtains prior Tribunal approval under s. 218 before suspending an employee who cooperated, on independent grounds of proven misconduct. The statutory bar is satisfied by the approval.

hypotheticals.question: Does s. 218 prevent the company from ever disciplining any employee while any investigation is pending?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. The protection is for employees who have provided information during the investigation, and the bar is on specified adverse actions without prior Tribunal approval. It is not a blanket freeze on all employment decisions for all staff.

distinctions.title: Employee protection (s. 218) vs inspector powers (s. 217)
distinctions.left: Shield for cooperating employees against adverse employment action without Tribunal approval
distinctions.right: Inspector’s powers to compel production and examination

misconceptions.trap: The company may freely dismiss any employee during investigation because employment is a private contract.
misconceptions.correction: Section 218 expressly requires prior Tribunal approval before discharging, suspending or otherwise disadvantaging an employee who has provided information during the investigation, notwithstanding any other law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 218 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm investigation and employee cooperation. II. Identify proposed adverse action. III. Require prior Tribunal approval. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Investigation facts; cooperation; action taken; approval status; precise relief.

examTips: Anti-victimisation, not a total discipline freeze.
content.migrationNote: Substantive enhancement. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

learningObjectives: State the employee-protection rule under s. 218.
Explain the requirement of prior Tribunal approval.
enhancement.definition: Section 218 bars a company, during investigation, from discharging, suspending, demoting, punishing or disadvantaging an employee who has provided information, except with prior Tribunal approval.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Employees who assist statutory investigation are protected from retaliatory employment action without independent Tribunal scrutiny.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 218 is the anti-victimisation companion to inspector powers under s. 217.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm cooperation; test approval before adverse action.
